sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

Mr. Nishit A.Bhalodi, learned advocate for the petitioner states that the petitioner is before this Court with the prayer to quash and set aside the order passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Godhra in M.A.C.M.A. No.240 of 2022 dated 24.08.2022, where the learned Tribunal has rejected the application for restoration of the original M.A.C.P. No.2443 of 2000 at Godhra.

2. Mr. Bhalodi submitted that the issues were framed at Exhibit-8 on 24.09.2017, and on 28.11.2017,
the claim petition was dismissed observing that the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined claimant has never produced documentary evidence at the time of filing of the Claim Petition, and thereafter a notice was served upon the opponent;

however,

The claim petition came to be dismissed just believing that the claimant is not interested in proceedings with the matter, and it was observed that many opportunities have been given to produce the evidence, but has failed to do so.

3. Mr. Bhalodi submitted that only within a period of two months, the claim petition came to be dismissed, where the learned Tribunal was rather required to follow the rules and should have given the judgment on merits by placing reliance even on Form No.54.

Mr. Bhalodi further stated that after framing of issues, the learned Tribunal should have given a notice to the claimant to produce the evidence, and further stated that while dismissing the claim petition, the claimant was given a liberty to file the claim petition afresh without affecting the provisions of law of limitation; thus,
stated that NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined keeping that in view, the Tribunal was required to restore the matter, where M.A.C.M.A. No.240 of 2022 was filed with the prayer for restoration of the claim petition to be heard on merits, but the learned Tribunal has observed that the claim petition being M.A.C.P. No.2443 of 2000 was dismissed by passing a judgment on merits and therefore submitted that the petitioner should have raised a grievance by filing the appeal.
4. After having gone through the judgment of dismissal, it can be prima facie seen that the claim petition was not decided on merits, rather liberty was granted to the claimant to file the claim petition afresh, which itself suggests that the dismissal was not on merits.
5.

In the case of Mahendra Rathore v. Omkar Singh & Ors., reported in AIR 2002 SC 505, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that the Tribunals should have a justice oriented approach and not a too technical or pedantic approach is expected to be adopted NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined by the Courts, more so when the application sought for restoring for hearing is a claim case arising out of the motor accident.

entities.text: Mahendra Rathore v. Omkar Singh & Ors., reported in AIR 2002 SC 505
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Refusal on the part of the Tribunal to restore the claim petition to show indulgence has occasioned failure of justice.

5.1 in the case of Bharatbhai Narsinghbhai Chaudhary & Ors. v. Malek Rafik Malek Himantbhai Malek & Ors., reported in 2011 (2) GLR 1324, while considering the restoration application, it had been observed as under:-
"Under Rule 3, therefore, even if, neither party appears when the suit is called for hearing, it is not compulsory for the Court to dismiss the suit.

entities.text: Bharatbhai Narsinghbhai Chaudhary & Ors. v. Malek Rafik Malek Himantbhai Malek & Ors., reported in 2011 (2) GLR 1324
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court may adjourn the suit.
In the event of dismissal of suit, it is open to the plaintiff to apply for restoration of the suit and the Court may set aside the order of dismissal and restore the suit.

An order dismissing a suit for default of appearance of parties is not a "decree"
under Sec. 2(2), and hence, is not acceptable.

An order of dismissal of a suit based on erroneous application of Rule 3 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined can be said to be a "case decided" within the Balvantbhai Bhavsingbhai Koli vs Farooque Dastgir Hayat on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127071501/
2 meaning of Sec. 115 of the Code.

entities.text: Balvantbhai Bhavsingbhai Koli vs Farooque Dastgir Hayat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, where the Court has acted with illegality or with material irregularity in the exercise of jurisdiction, a revision would lie against such an order.

The provisions of the Code are applicable to govern the procedure in a Motor Accident Claim case as provided under Rule 229 of the Gujarat Motor Vehicles Rules,
1989.
There is no separate procedural law, made applicable to conduct the Motor Accident Claim petitions.

Therefore, application for restoration, made under Order 9,
Rule 4, in the instant case, is absolute, legal and sustainable, and therefore, the revision arisen out of such order, passed below such application is also undoubtedly maintainable."

5.2 The learned Tribunal could have followed the judgment in the case of Jai Prakash Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. reported in (2010) 2 SCC 607 and could have decided the compensation relying upon Form-54.

entities.text: Jai Prakash Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. reported in (2010) 2 SCC 607
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of Bharatbhai Narsinghbhai NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined Chaudhary (supra), it has been further held as under:-
"The Act and the Rules framed thereunder also do not empower the Claims Tribunal to dispose an application merely for default of the applicant without arriving at findings on merits of the case, after the stage of framing issues.

entities.text: Bharatbhai Narsinghbhai NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED:
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the instant case,
issues were framed, and thereafter, the learned Tribunal was required to decide the case on merits with a view to provide substantial justice instead of entering into the technicalities."
6.
The Tribunal ought to have kept in mind that the rules are made to strengthen the powers of the Court/ Tribunal.
Every effort should be made to hear on merits after the stage of framing of issues.
The Courts are lauded as they are to do substantial justice.

Even if the matter gets dismissed for default on some technical ground or because of some carelessness or inability or inadvertence of the applicant, the Claims Tribunal can be informed of the social object of the Motor Vehicle Act and should have condoned such acts of the applicant and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/5151/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 undefined ought to have restored the matter for hearing on merits.

7. Thus, in view of the above, the order dated 24.08.2022 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Godhra in M.A.C.M.A. No.240 of 2022 is quashed and set aside and the matter is ordered to be restored in the file of the concerned Tribunal with direction that the same may be decided within a period of 6 weeks.
8. Accordingly, the present petition stands disposed of.
